items.what: Table 2 extracted with damaged column alignment; bold/underline (best/second best) marks lost. Columns reconstructed by AUTHOR and cross-checked against Table 4, findings 4-6 and the 16/18 win count.
items.impact: Values in E011 are 'reconstructed'; the paper reports best/second-best marks only through the lost formatting, so the draft does not claim per-dataset winners.

items.what: No seeds, variance, or confidence intervals for any result (authors: models are public checkpoints, retraining infeasible).
items.impact: All performance differences are single-evaluation point values; no significance claims are possible. Recorded as limitation L005.

items.what: Aggregation formula for 'Avg. Performance vs. BM25' is not defined in the extracted text.
items.impact: Reported as printed and described only as the paper's summary row.

items.what: Table 3 latency columns damaged (GPU/CPU cells misaligned).
items.impact: Only prose-level latency statements and the index sizes are used.

items.what: Table 10 shows only three datasets of the cosine vs dot-product comparison, while the text says dot-product is worse on a majority of other datasets.
items.impact: The draft reports the three tabulated datasets and attributes the 'majority' statement to the text.

items.what: Figure 2 heatmap values, Figure 3 bar values and Figures 4-5 distributions are not reliably extracted.
items.impact: No numbers taken from figures except those repeated in prose.

items.what: No ablation isolating why TAS-B generalizes better or why cross-attention helps.
Rationale for choosing exactly these ten systems is only partly stated ('diverse, recent, state-of-the-art, focus on transformer-based').
items.impact: Stated as the authors state it; no invented rationale.
